AI.motivation: To improve the design and analytical approaches for future SKAO observations based on past experiences with CD and EoR.
AI.method: Developing accurate simulation pipelines and calibrating methods to address systematic issues like sky model limitations and antenna interactions.
AI.result: A summary of various approaches taken by research groups to enhance observation accuracy and mitigate systematic effects.
AI.conclusion: The findings inform the design and analysis of future SKAO observations.

title: Accreting Compact Object Binaries with the SKA
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII), 2026 (arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no:AASKAII/Beri01. Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII) outlines the transformative scientific advances that will be enabled by the SKA telescopes
summary: Accreting binary systems provide a time-resolved view of the accretion and ejection processes that are seen in all classes of compact objects, from stellar-mass to supermassive. They allow us to study the launching of relativistic jets on human timescales, probing how the jets are coupled to the underlying accretion flow, and providing unique insights that can be extended to supermassive black holes via the well-established mass scale invariance. Comparative studies of jets from different classes of compact objects allow us to determine the impact of mass, spin, magnetic fields, and stellar surfaces on the launching of jets. The jets from black hole X-ray binaries provide probes of the Galactic black hole population, and an important source of feedback to the surrounding interstellar medium. While existing radio facilities (including the SKA precursors) have made great progress in this field in recent years, the SKA will enhance such studies via its high point source and surface brightness sensitivity, high angular resolution, and broad frequency coverage. This will enable the extension of our existing black hole studies to the fainter accreting neutron star and white dwarf population, the detection of previously-undiscovered systems in a low-luminosity quiescent state, and the extension of our studies to nearby galaxies, revealing rare, high-accretion rate systems that probe a key phase of black hole growth.

AI.tldr: Accreting binary systems are crucial for studying accretion and jet processes in compact objects, with the SKA enhancing our understanding across various classes.
AI.motivation: The study of accreting binary systems is vital for understanding the dynamics of accretion and ejection processes across different classes of compact objects.
AI.method: Comparative analysis of jets in different compact objects to assess the influences of mass, spin, magnetic fields, and stellar surfaces, supported by advanced observations from the SKA.
AI.result: Enhanced capabilities of the SKA will allow the detection of fainter systems and help expand knowledge of black hole populations and feedback mechanisms in the interstellar medium.
AI.conclusion: The SKA will significantly advance our understanding of accreting neutron stars and white dwarfs, revealing essential aspects of black hole growth and evolution.

title: Hybrid radio and particle detection of air showers: potential for ultra-high-energy photon identification
comment: 32 pages, 24 figures. Prepared for submission to JCAP
summary: The autonomous radio-detection of extensive air showers initiated by ultra-high-energy (UHE) particles arriving with very inclined zenith angles has seen significant advancements in recent years, with several large-scale surface arrays planned and prototypes already in operation. In this work, we examine whether these radio detectors, supplemented by scintillators, could serve as competitive UHE photon detectors. Indeed, for inclined showers, radio emissions can be detected by antennas for both cosmic-ray and photon primaries, while the muon-rich signatures of the former would typically trigger the scintillators. Using two key observables -- the total root mean square of the radio signal and the total energy deposit recorded in the scintillators -- we show that effective separation between the two types of showers could be achieved in a hybrid radio antenna and scintillator setup. As a case study, we apply this method to a hypothetical hybrid array of radio antennas, complemented by Telescope Array-like scintillators, with the layout of the prototype of the Giant Radio Array for Neutrino Detection (GRAND), GRANDProto300. Our estimates show that such a hybrid array could set competitive upper limits on the integral photon flux in the energy range of approximately 0.3 to 3 EeV.

AI.tldr: This study explores the potential of hybrid radio and scintillator detectors for differentiating between extensive air showers from ultra-high-energy photons and cosmic rays, demonstrating the effectiveness of this method using a proposed setup.
AI.motivation: The motivation behind this work is to investigate the capabilities of hybrid radio detectors, supported by scintillators, in detecting ultra-high-energy (UHE) photons, especially for air showers with inclined zenith angles.
AI.method: The study utilizes two key observables: the total root mean square of the radio signal and the energy deposit recorded in scintillators, to distinguish between cosmic-ray and photon-induced air showers.
AI.result: The analysis indicates that effective separation between the two types of showers can be achieved using a hybrid setup of radio antennas and scintillators, exemplified by a case study on a proposed hybrid array configuration.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest that such a hybrid array could provide competitive upper limits on the integral photon flux in the energy range of 0.3 to 3 EeV.

title: Compact Objects Revealed by SKA and SKA-VLBI
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII), 2026(arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no:AASKAII/Lin01
summary: Compact objects represent a crucial interdisciplinary frontier between astronomy and fundamental physics.The SKA/SKA-VLBI, with exceptional sensitivity (at $μ$Jy levels) and ultrahigh positional precision (at $μ$as levels), will enable direct, precise measurements of orbital dynamics in compact objects including black holes and neutron stars. This facility is expected to achieve at least three breakthroughs: (1) Developing effective methodologies for detecting and identifying black hole-neutron star binaries to construct observational catalogues, thus advancing investigations into the equation of state of ultra-dense nuclear matter and strong-field relativistic effects; (2) Determining critical parameters such as orbital elements and component masses in compact binaries, yielding insights into stellar structures and evolutionary mechanisms under extreme conditions; (3) Identifying intermediate-mass black holes and measuring their masses to deepen understanding of black hole formation and evolution.

AI.tldr: The SKA will facilitate groundbreaking research on compact objects through precise measurements and methods for black hole-neutron star binaries and intermediate-mass black holes.
AI.motivation: To explore the connection between astronomy and fundamental physics by studying compact objects.
AI.method: Utilizing the SKA/SKA-VLBI for high-sensitivity and high-precision measurements of orbital dynamics.
AI.result: Identification of black hole-neutron star binaries and measurement of orbital parameters and intermediate-mass black holes.
AI.conclusion: The SKA is poised to significantly enhance our understanding of ultra-dense nuclear matter, stellar structures, and the evolution of black holes.

title: Probing Physical Conditions in Classical and Symbiotic Novae with the Square Kilometre Array Observatory
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII), 2026 (arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no:AASKAII/Lico01. Advancing Astrophysics with the SKAII (AASKAII) outlines the transformative scientific advances that will be enabled by the SKA telescopes
summary: Cataclysmic variables and symbiotic stars are interacting binary systems in which a hot white dwarf (WD) orbits a companion main-sequence or red giant star, respectively. Accumulation of hydrogen-rich material on the WD surface may trigger re-ignition of thermonuclear reactions that, under degenerate conditions, lead to an explosive ejection of the accreted layer mixed with WD material. These explosions, known as classical novae, provide opportunities to study key astrophysical processes such as binary evolution, accretion, ionisation of circumstellar material, mass ejection, jet formation, and thermonuclear burning. Radio emission in these systems arises from both thermal and non-thermal processes, which manifest differently in classical and symbiotic novae. $γ$-ray emission has also been detected in several cases, and recent progress, driven by coordinated radio and multiwavelength observations, has greatly advanced our understanding of both types of novae. Multi-frequency, multi-epoch, and multi-scale interferometric observations are powerful probes of the evolving physical conditions following thermonuclear explosions, revealing information from both ionised and relativistic particle populations. The SKAO, particularly its SKA-Mid component, will enable regular monitoring of Galactic novae, multiple times per year for classical novae and every few years for symbiotic systems. It will explore a wide range of conditions, including companion types, WD masses, accretion regimes, and surrounding environments. The VLBI capabilities of the SKAO will target compact shocked regions, while its exceptional sensitivity will also allow characterisation of emission during quiescent phases of the binaries.

AI.tldr: The study of cataclysmic variables and symbiotic stars focuses on classical novae and their thermonuclear explosions, utilizing advanced radio and multiwavelength observations for insights into astrophysical processes, with the SKAO enhancing monitoring and characterisation of these systems.
AI.motivation: To investigate the astrophysical processes related to classical novae, including binary evolution and mass ejection, through detailed observational studies.
AI.method: Employ multi-frequency, multi-epoch, and multi-scale interferometric observations, leveraging the SKAO, particularly SKA-Mid, for monitoring Galactic novae and characterising emissions.
AI.result: Recent progress has enhanced understanding of classical and symbiotic novae through coordinated observations, revealing dynamics of thermonuclear explosions and their aftermaths.
AI.conclusion: The SKAO will significantly improve ongoing monitoring and characterization of various binary systems, providing comprehensive data on their physical conditions.

title: Observation of A Solar Like Magnetic Reconnection Event in an AGN Corona with XRISM
comment: Submitted to APJL
summary: The X-ray source in AGN is commonly referred to as the corona by analogy to stellar coronae. The similarities between the two suggest that the heating mechanism of AGN coronae is magnetic reconnection -- as in cool stars -- but this has not yet been directly observed. This work presents the first observational evidence for a magnetic reconnection flare in an AGN corona. We report on a flare in NGC 3783, which was observed with XRISM/Xtend and XMM-Newton/EPIC-PN exhibiting distinct temporal evolution in soft ($<2.0\,$keV) and hard ($>2.0\,$keV) X-rays. An Ultra-Fast Outflow (UFO) was detected during the event. The flare features the Neupert effect -- a temporal signature widely observed in the Sun, which shows that the flare is powered by magnetic reconnection, with the UFO playing a role analogous to a solar Coronal Mass Ejection (CME). We derive an upper limit of $30 \, R_g$ on the height of the magnetic loop from which the flare originates. Using the UFO's measured properties to characterize the magnetic field, we obtain $B > 1.3 \times 10^4\,$G for the field annihilated during the flare from total energy considerations, and $B \approx 500\,$G for the momentary magnetic field during reconnection from a dynamical consideration.

AI.tldr: This study provides the first observational evidence of magnetic reconnection in the corona of an active galactic nucleus (AGN) through a flare observed in NGC 3783.
AI.motivation: To investigate the heating mechanism of AGN coronae, which is suggested to be magnetic reconnection akin to that observed in stellar coronae, despite lack of direct evidence.
AI.method: The study involved observational data from XRISM/Xtend and XMM-Newton/EPIC-PN, focusing on a flare in NGC 3783 with analysis of soft and hard X-rays, and detection of an Ultra-Fast Outflow (UFO).
AI.result: The flare exhibited distinct differences in X-ray temporal evolution and demonstrated the Neupert effect, indicating magnetic reconnection involvement, with the UFO comparable to a solar Coronal Mass Ejection (CME).
AI.conclusion: The study establishes that the observed magnetic reconnection flare in AGN coronae supports the hypothesis of magnetic reconnection as the heating mechanism, with quantifiable magnetic field strengths derived.

title: A magnetically-supported disk-corona model for Changing-Look AGN transitions
comment: 10 pages, 6 figures, 1 table, Submitted to ApJL
summary: Changing-Look Active Galactic Nuclei (CLAGN) undergo dramatic spectral and luminosity transitions on timescales of months to a few years -- orders of magnitude shorter than the viscous timescale of a standard $α$-disk at the radii where the optical/UV continuum is generated, for typical supermassive black hole masses. We show that a magnetically supported disk-corona model reproduces \emph{both} the observed Eddington ratio at which changing event occurs and the observed transition duration. Using the \texttt{diskvert} code, which solves the steady vertical structure under simultaneous gas, radiation and magnetic pressure support with a self-consistent warm corona, we (i) construct thermal-viscous S-curves, and (ii) calculate the integrated thermal timescale together with the front propagation timescale. We compute a large grid of models of different black hole masses, Eddington ratios, magnetic viscosities, and disk radii, showing that magnetized disks push the S-curve knee down to an Eddington ratio of $ \approx 0.01-0.03$, and introduce a new stable branch of high luminosity solutions, while the limit-cycle timescale enters the months-to-years range for $M_\mathrm{BH} = 10^{7}-10^{9}\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$. Confronted with a sample of five CLAGN (Mkn 590, NGC 1566, IRAS 23226$-$3843, Mkn 1018, NGC 2617), the model jointly reproduces the empirical Eddington rates and the observed event durations only when the inner disk is strongly magnetized. The case of Mkn 590 is especially constraining: the recent tightly-determined transition Eddington ratio is matched by a highly magnetized disk-corona flow at small radii.

AI.tldr: This study presents a model that explains the rapid transitions in Changing-Look Active Galactic Nuclei (CLAGN) using magnetically supported disk-corona mechanisms, validating its predictions against observational data.
AI.motivation: To understand the phenomenon of rapid spectral and luminosity transitions in CLAGN, impacting our knowledge of supermassive black holes.
AI.method: A magnetically supported disk-corona model is used alongside the 	exttt{diskvert} code to analyze the vertical structure of the disk under gas, radiation, and magnetic pressure support, and to compute S-curves and timescales.
AI.result: The model shows that magnetized disks lower the S-curve knee Eddington ratio to about 0.01-0.03 and creates a stable, high luminosity branch, fitting observations for black hole masses between $10^{7}$ and $10^{9}\,	ext{M}_	ext{o}$ and transition durations in the months-to-years range.
AI.conclusion: For the examined CLAGN sample, strong magnetization in the inner disk is essential to reproduce observed Eddington rates and transition durations, particularly for Mkn 590.

title: Multi-Band Optical Variability of Blazar 1ES 2344+514 on Diverse Time-Scales
comment: 18 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables. Published in "Journal of Advanced Research in Natural and Applied Sciences" supported by Canakkale Onsekiz Mart University
summary: This study presents the results of multi-band observations from 2022 to 2024 and Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) observations from 2018 to 2023, examining the flux variability of the blazar 1ES 2344+514 on diverse time-scales in the optical bands. The blazar has mild short-term variability (STV) and long-term variability (LTV), with small amplitudes of $\sim0.7$ mag and 0.4 mag for the host subtracted- and included-light curves, respectively. The power-enhanced F-test and the nested Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) statistical tests of the six intra-day light curves show that the blazar has no minute-scale variability. The multiband color behavior analysis revealed a moderate redder-when-brighter (RWB) trend on intra-day time scales, while the LTV shows no detectable color behavior. We found a strong correlation between the ZTF optical light curves without any time lag, but no detectable correlations for the optical band emissions. From our periodicity searches using WWZ and LS methods, three significant quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) signals in the ZTF light curves are found at about 1.02, 1.3, and 2.85 years. The observational results indicate that the blazar 1ES 2344+514 has a complex variability while emphasizing the need for future observations to unravel its underlying mechanisms.

AI.tldr: The study analyzes the flux variability of the blazar 1ES 2344+514 using multi-band observations and ZTF data, highlighting its complex variability patterns over short and long timescales.
AI.motivation: To investigate the flux variability of the blazar 1ES 2344+514 across different optical bands and time scales.
AI.method: Utilization of multi-band observations from 2022-2024 and ZTF data from 2018-2023, along with statistical tests (F-test, ANOVA) and periodicity analysis (WWZ, LS methods).
AI.result: The blazar exhibits mild short-term and long-term variability with no minute-scale variability, a moderate RWB trend on intra-day scales, and significant QPO signals at 1.02, 1.3, and 2.85 years.
AI.conclusion: The results indicate the complexity of 1ES 2344+514's variability, suggesting a need for further observations to understand its mechanisms.

title: Study for curvature radiation and magnetic pair creation process on polar-cap region of magnetic white dwarf
comment: 18 pages, 8 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary:
Rapidly rotating, strongly magnetized white dwarfs (WDs) have been proposed as potential sites of rotation-powered activity analogous to that of a neutron star pulsar. In this study, we investigate particle acceleration, radiation processes, pair creation and resulting synchrotron radiation in the polar cap acceleration region.
  Within the framework of the space-charge-limited flow model, we examine how these processes depend on the spin period and surface magnetic field using both one-dimensional numerical calculations and analytical estimates.
  To explore the impact of the magnetic field geometry on the accelerating process, we consider both a pure dipole field and a combination of dipole and quadrupole fields.
  The inclusion of a quadrupole component reduces the curvature radius of the magnetic field lines, and significantly enhances the accelerating field, leading to more efficient radiation and pair creation processes. Using this framework, we evaluate the WD death line with a more consistent treatment of the relevant physical processes than the previous studies.
  We find that the pair creation process can occur for spin periods $P\lesssim100$~s, when the dipole field strength $B_{*,d}\lesssim10^{10}$~G, indicating that pair creation is difficult to sustain in currently known magnetic WDs. We discuss the implications of our model for rotation-powered activity in rapidly spinning isolated magnetic WDs and for the possible WD interpretation of long-period radio transients.

AI.tldr: This study investigates radiation processes and pair creation in rapidly rotating, magnetized white dwarfs (WDs), focusing on the effects of magnetic field geometry using numerical and analytical methods.
AI.motivation: The paper explores the potential of rapidly rotating, strongly magnetized WDs to exhibit activities similar to neutron star pulsars, particularly in particle acceleration and radiation.
AI.method: Using a space-charge-limited flow model, the study assesses the effects of spin period and surface magnetic field on particle acceleration and radiation, including both dipole and quadrupole field configurations in one-dimensional numerical and analytical calculations.
AI.result: The inclusion of a quadrupole magnetic field significantly enhances the accelerating field, allowing for more efficient radiation and pair creation processes, revealing a WD death line under certain magnetic conditions.
AI.conclusion: Pair creation is possible for spin periods less than 100 seconds and dipole field strengths under 10^10 G, suggesting that sustaining pair creation is challenging in observed magnetic WDs, with implications for understanding rotation-powered activities and long-period radio transients.

title: Broadband multiwavelength properties of the archetypal blazar 3C 279 during the 2017 Event Horizon Telescope campaign
comment: 29 pages, 13 figures, accepted by Astronomy & Astrophysics on June 18, 2026
summary: The archetypal blazar 3C 279 hosts a prominent relativistic jet and exhibits strong broadband variability across the electromagnetic spectrum. In April 2017, the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) observed 3C 279, alongside one of the most extensive quasi-simultaneous multiwavelength (MWL) campaigns ever conducted. With the aim of investigating the physical processes governing 3C 279, we analyzed individual observations and multiband light curves, and constructed a new quasi-simultaneous MWL spectrum. We also performed phenomenological modeling using the turbulent extreme multi-zone (TEMZ) model to constrain the fundamental physical properties of the source. The EHT observations reveal a clear flux increase in the innermost core between April 5 and 11, 2017. Over a broader timescale, radio measurements at longer wavelengths show concurrent enhancements in core flux and polarization around mid-April, coinciding with the ejection of a superluminal knot. Record UV-optical flares with strong polarization variability occurred in late March, followed by gamma-ray activity that declined before the end of the EHT observing period. During this interval, the source remained in a low X-ray state and showed no detectable VHE emission. The TEMZ modeling suggests that the broadband spectrum and variability of 3C 279 can be explained within a jet scenario in which turbulent plasma cells are compressed by a stationary conical shock. However, alternative interpretations, such as magnetic reconnection or a moving shock-in-jet event, remain plausible. This coordinated MWL campaign advances our understanding of the origin of jet and gamma-ray emission in 3C 279, while also providing a comprehensive publicly available dataset that will serve as a valuable reference for future studies.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the variability of the blazar 3C 279 through multiwavelength observations and modeling, revealing critical insights into jet dynamics and emission mechanisms.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical processes governing the blazar 3C 279 and its electromagnetic variability.
AI.method: A coordinated multiwavelength campaign was conducted alongside EHT observations, involving light curve analysis and the turbulent extreme multi-zone (TEMZ) model for phenomenological modeling.
AI.result: The observations showed significant flux variations, including a clear increase in the innermost core and variations in polarization, with gamma-ray activity preceding the EHT observations' end.
AI.conclusion: The results support a jet scenario with compressed turbulent plasma, while acknowledging alternative models, enhancing understanding of jet and gamma-ray emission in 3C 279.

title: Two years of shock interaction tracing three phases of evolution: the explosion of a Type IIn supernova, SN 2019vxm
comment: Submitted to ApJ. 26 pages, 17 figures, 6 tables. Comments are welcome
summary: We present multi-wavelength photometric and optical spectroscopic observations of the long-lived interacting supernova SN 2019vxm, spanning more than two years after the explosion. SN 2019vxm is a slowly rising (rise time ~ 45.9 days in the R-band), slowly declining supernova reaching an R-band peak absolute magnitude of ~-20.3 mag. The SN light curve post-maximum shows a shallow decline, followed by a secondary, steeper decline in the optical (0.01 mag/day), with late-time IR brightening. The total radiated luminosity is 5x10^50 erg, placing it among the energetic class of its type. We estimated a CSM mass of 3-8 M_sun through light-curve modeling (independent of the CSM density profile) and by comparison with theoretical models. We estimate a minimum ejecta mass of ~ 3.88 M_sun from the broad H-alpha component, consistent with the ejecta mass obtained from the light curve models. The solely interaction-dominated initial epochs are later accompanied by photon-scattering signatures, leading to asymmetric line profiles with symmetric wings. The late phase, characterized by enhanced brightness at longer wavelengths and a stronger asymmetric line profile with the red side flux strongly suppressed, indicates the influence of pre-existing or newly formed dust with temperatures ~ 1500 K at ~4x10^16 cm. Even in the late phases, no nebular lines are present in the spectra, indicating dense or obscured ejecta.

AI.tldr: The study investigates the supernova SN 2019vxm through two years of multi-wavelength observations, revealing key characteristics such as slow rise and decline, high luminosity, significant circumstellar material, and evidence of dust formation.
AI.motivation: To understand the evolution and properties of the long-lived interacting supernova SN 2019vxm, focusing on its photometric and spectroscopic behavior over an extended observational period.
AI.method: Multi-wavelength photometric and optical spectroscopic observations are analyzed, including light-curve modeling and comparisons with theoretical models to estimate the parameters of the supernova.
AI.result: The analysis reveals an R-band peak absolute magnitude of ~-20.3, a total radiated luminosity of 5x10^50 erg, and circumstellar material mass estimates of 3-8 M_sun, alongside signs of dust formation in the late phase.
AI.conclusion: SN 2019vxm presents as an energetic supernova with unique interaction-dominated phases and signs of dust influence, indicating complex underlying ejecta conditions.

title: UsingSKA-Low to Detect PeV Gamma-rays from Galactic Sources
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKAII(AASKAII), 2026(arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no:AASKAII/Nelles01
summary: Detecting so called PeVatrons is considered one of the prime goals of $γ$-ray astronomy. PeVatrons are astrophysical objects in the Galaxy that are sources of cosmic rays exceeding PeV ($10^{15}$ eV) energies, the highest in our Galaxy. Their nature is unknown as of now, with some candidates reaching barely above PeV energies just having been identified. Serendipitously, the energy threshold of air shower detection using radio emission, has been proven at 50 PeV. There is a case to be made that SKA-Low with its unprecedented number of antennas, can reach lower in energy, while the size of the core is sufficiently large provide a significant effective area to measure PeV fluxes. While this promises a novel angle towards understanding the cosmic ray accelerators in our Galaxy, it also would be the first detection of $γ$-ray air showers using radio emission.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses the detection of PeVatrons, high-energy cosmic ray sources in the Galaxy, proposing that SKA-Low can effectively measure air showers at lower energies than previously possible.
AI.motivation: Identifying PeVatrons is crucial for understanding cosmic ray origins and the extreme energy processes in our Galaxy.
AI.method: Utilizing SKA-Low's extensive antenna array to detect radio emissions from air showers, aiming to lower the energy threshold for detection while measuring PeV fluxes.
AI.result: SKA-Low could enable the detection of PeV air showers, potentially leading to new insights into cosmic ray accelerators.
AI.conclusion: This approach represents a novel method for $γ$-ray astronomy, enhancing our knowledge about high-energy astrophysical phenomena.
